# Red Mountain (Hendrickson Construction), Aspen CO

<!-- Generated by examples/red-mountain/build.ts from facts.json. Edit the JSON and rebuild. -->

**Type:** Luxury mountain residence, three stories of glass between sandstone piers under deep cedar soffits  
**Location:** Red Mountain, Aspen, Colorado (exact address not published)

A house built by Hendrickson Construction and published as "Red Mountain" in its project gallery. The builder publishes photos and a one-line description only: no architect, no floor area, no plans. Every dimension below was read from the builder's dusk hero photo by an earlier build, or is an estimate. This is not the CCY Architects concrete house of the same name.

## Estimates

Each of these is a modelling assumption, not a published number.

| Assumption | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Boulder retaining wall at the far left (line, thickness, height) | x -84, z -24..34; 2.5 thick, 4 high ft | **Estimate.** The hero photo shows a boulder retaining wall at the far left edge of the lawn (earlier reading); its line, length and size are estimates. Pascal has no boulder kind, so it is a stone-faced wall. |
| Lawn extent | x -120..120, z -90..120 ft | **Estimate.** The photo shows lawn beyond the terrace; its extent is not visible and is set large enough to fill every camera view. |
| Back and far-left facades (glass spans in plan coordinates) | L1 back x -38..-24, 12..26, 32..40; wing back x -66..-56; wing left z 0..12; L2 back x -34..-20, 14..28; L2 left z -4..8; L3 back x -32..-18, 12..24; L3 left z -4..8 ft | **Estimate.** Invented: these facades are not in any published photo. They are mostly stone with a few glass bays so the house reads complete from every side. |
| Exterior wall thickness, levels 1 / 2 / 3 | 1.5, 1.3, 1.3 ft | **Estimate.** Ledgestone veneer over a framed wall. Sets how deep the glass sits behind the stone face. |
| Glass rail height | 3.5 ft | **Estimate.** 42 in, a common guard height for frameless glass rails; the photo shows rails but their height cannot be measured. |
| Stone band above each glass bay | 0.07 m | **Estimate.** A Pascal window must fit under its wall top, so floor-to-ceiling glass stops 7 cm below the slab soffit. It reads as the head of the frame. |
| Interior rooms | L1: stair hall, great room, kitchen, guest wing; L2: stair hall, bedrooms, primary suite; L3: stair hall, family room, bunk room | **Estimate.** Invented: the gallery shows bedrooms, living rooms, a kitchen, a gym and baths, but no plan. One stair hall stacks through all three floors; the remaining rooms are placeholders. |
| Stairs | two straight flights, 3.6 ft wide, side by side in a 12 ft stair hall at x -6..6, z -26..2 ft | **Estimate.** Invented: no plan is published. Level 1 to 2 climbs toward the front, level 2 to 3 climbs back. |

## Conflicts and notes

- Two different Aspen houses are published as "Red Mountain". This scene is the Hendrickson Construction house (hendricksoninc.com/our-work/red-mountain). It is NOT CCY Architects' concrete Red Mountain residence: none of CCY's numbers or palette (7,198 SF, board-formed concrete, steel, Swiss Pearl panels, hillside terracing) are used here.
- No floor area is published for the Hendrickson house. The gross floor area in the stats above is what this model measures: the outer footprint of each storey, summed.
- Wall sconces on the piers (visible in the photo) are not modelled: Pascal's item library has no light fixture, and a scripted object (add_object) needs script compilation, which the in-process build does not enable.
- Stone finish: the library stone (flooring-wallstone1) renders orange-brown, too dark for the photo's light warm sandstone. sandstone.jpg is that same library texture, recoloured onto a tan-cream ramp (#b58a5c courses, #d9bf93 to #e2cba2 faces). It is embedded in the scene as the scene material mat_sandstone (a data:image albedo) and painted on every exterior wall face, the terrace edges and both chimneys.
- The roof is modelled flat; the photo reads as low-slope (nearly flat), so the pitch is below what the photo can show.
